title: S1 V3.9 Bollinger %B at entry — the strongest effect in the programme, and why it is not a filter
question: S1 V3.9's entry Bollinger %B shows a monotone win-rate gradient topping at 73.17% for entries above the upper band against a 55.93% baseline. Does it survive the screens that reduced every other candidate in this programme to an artefact, and if it does, is filtering on it worth anything after opportunity cost?
hypothesis: That the gradient is real — it has a mechanism, unlike the candidates that failed — and that filtering on it will nevertheless destroy return, because the programme has already established that win rate is purchasable.

findings.title: The gradient is real, and it is the first thing in this programme to clear every screen
findings.detail: Entries above the upper band win 73.17% on 82 trades against a 55.93% baseline — a 20.86-point gap where the smallest gap these samples could resolve is 16.9. Family permutation across all seven buckets gives p=0.003 with an observed max |t| of 3.14 against a null median of 1.37. A moving-block bootstrap puts the 90% interval at 10.96 to 29.64 points, excluding zero in every one of 4000 resamples. Nothing else in twenty-four studies has done this.

findings.title: It strengthens out of sample while the strategy itself decays
findings.detail: Above-upper win rate runs 65.12% on train (n=43), 81.25% on validation (n=16) and 82.61% on holdout (n=23). Over the same three periods the baseline goes 56.76%, 57.63%, 51.58% — the strategy got worse and this bucket got better. That is the opposite of the overfitting signature: RS-XAUUSD-20260819-001's slot basket ran Sharpe 3.07 to -2.12 across the same kind of split.

findings.title: The response is continuous, so it is not a bucketing artefact
findings.detail: Sorted into %B deciles the win rate rises from 36.17% in the lowest to 81.25% in the highest, Spearman 0.839. It also keeps rising *inside* the above-upper bucket: the lower half of those 82 trades wins 65.85% and the upper half 80.49%. A real gradient does that; an effect manufactured by where a boundary was drawn shows a step at the boundary and flatness either side of it.

findings.title: It survives the momentum it could have been a proxy for
findings.detail: Closing outside the band is itself a strong move, so the obvious deflation is that the band is measuring momentum. Split by six-bar entry momentum, the above-upper advantage holds in all three terciles: +8.8 points in the lowest, +14.21 in the middle, +21.93 in the highest. It does grow with momentum, so the two are not independent — but the band adds something at every level of it rather than only where momentum is already extreme.

findings.title: Filtering on it destroys more return than it saves, and the two objectives point at different thresholds
findings.detail: Requiring %B above 1.0 lifts win rate to 73.17% and profit factor to 4.541 — while keeping 17.4% of the entries and 44.0% of the total return. Push it to 1.1 and win rate reaches 79.59% on 10.4% of trades and 30.6% of the return. The threshold that maximises total return is 0.4, which filters almost nothing (94.9% kept) for +4.4% return, itself well inside noise. Best win rate and best return do not agree at any threshold tested.

findings.title: This is the same lesson RS-XAUUSD-20260818-001 already paid for
findings.detail: That study lifted S1 to 88.6% win rate with a take-profit overlay and cut return from +88.6% to between +14% and +36%. Here the mechanism is different — discarding entries rather than truncating winners — and the arithmetic lands in the same place. A rule that raises win rate by taking fewer trades has to be judged in return, and when it is, this one loses.

findings.title: The prior table understated it because it saw a third of the trades
findings.detail: RS-XAUUSD-20260727-001 joined %B for 165 of its 450 trades and reported above_upper at 79.31% on n=29. On the full 472 with complete coverage the figure is 73.17% on n=82 — lower, and far better evidenced. Its neighbouring buckets moved too: near_middle went from 28.0% on n=25 to 40.74% on n=81. The direction survived triple the sample; the extremes were small-sample noise.

findings.title: An unprompted impression, the Pine tooltip and the data agree, and that is why it was worth testing
findings.detail: An unprompted impression that signals high in the band win more often. V3.9's Pine already carries a disabled use_bb_filter whose tooltip records a 77.8% win rate for entries above the upper band. Neither is evidence — a tooltip is not a study and an impression is not a sample — but three independent statements of the same claim justified spending the screens on it rather than dismissing it with the others.

findings.title: Its value is as information at decision time, not as a gate
findings.detail: Everything above points the same way: %B genuinely separates outcomes, and acting on it by refusing entries costs money. That is precisely the shape of a number that belongs in front of a human who is deciding, and does not belong in the strategy. It is already displayed that way in the signal-feedback message, with its sample size attached and no recommendation.

card_summary: Bollinger %B at entry clears every screen in the programme — and filtering on it still loses money.
